title: ebben a házban: this and that with endings

sections.title: The ending goes on both words
sections.content: You know *ez* and *az* ("this" and "that") and the endings *-ban/-ben*, *-ba/-be*, *-ból/-ből* and *-val/-vel*. When a noun with *a/az* takes an ending, the demonstrative takes the same ending too, and the *a/az* stays in between: *ebben a házban* ("in this house"), *abban a boltban* ("in that shop"). The noun and the demonstrative agree in case, and you cannot leave the ending off the demonstrative.

sections.title: this and that with six endings

in this house / in that house

ebből a boltból / abból a boltból

ehhez a parkhoz / ahhoz a parkhoz

ezzel a busszal / azzal a busszal

sections.title: The z changes
sections.content: In *ez* and *az* the final *z* turns into the first sound of the ending: *ez* + *-ban* is *ebben*, *ez* + *-hoz* is *ehhez*, *az* + *-val* is *azzal*, *az* + *-ból* is *abból*. This is the same kind of change you know from *-val/-vel* (*busszal*). The only ending here that does not change the *z* is *-n*: *ezen*, *azon*. The demonstrative follows its own vowel harmony (*ehhez*, *ahhoz*), and the noun follows its own (*parkhoz*), so the two endings can differ.

items.english: There is bread in that shop.
I am coming out of this shop.
We are going to this park.

items.spanish: Ezen a téren van egy szobor.
items.english: There is a statue on this square.
I am going by that bus.

sections.content: Put the ending on both words: once on *ez/az*, once on the noun. *Ez a házban* is wrong, and so is *ebben a ház*.
